content.title: About
content.content: Millet is a whole grain that has been puffed, making it light and crunchy. It has a mild nutty flavor and is commonly used in breakfast cereals, muesli, baking, and as a healthy snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Millet is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for over 5,000 years in Africa and Asia.
Puffing is achieved by rapidly heating the grains under high pressure, causing them to “explode.”
Millet is naturally gluten‑free, making it suitable for gluten‑free diets.
It is a staple in traditional dishes across Africa, Asia, and Eastern Europe.
Puffed millet retains most of the nutrients of the original grain.

items.title: Rich in magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function and participates in energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Iron is essential for hemoglobin formation and oxygen transport in the body.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Millet raises blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to millet.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking or fermenting can mitigate this.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Commercial puffed millet may contain added sugar, salt, or flavorings.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed millet can be eaten as a snack, added to muesli, yogurt, smoothies, baked into breads, bars, and muffins. It is also used in gluten‑free recipes as a wheat substitute.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to maintain crunch and prevent rancidity.
